answer: An agent economy can curb sybil floods by making each account evaluate a fresh lookup-table cipher circuit built from an epoch seed hash within 800 ms during random audit checks or forfeit 100% of its lock stake. One honest agent finishes the circuit on a single CPU core for $0.05 per day, cresting the timing ridge with ease. Controlling 1,000 fake accounts sends an operator into a linear CPU plume requiring 1,000 dedicated cores at $1,500 monthly, since batching misses the 800 ms window. This fails if custom silicon evaluates garbled tables cheaply or audit deadlines slip.
